summary.headline: Alembic Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to INR2,603 crore; FY27 growth guidance raised to 20-25% from mid-teens.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36% YoY to INR2,603 crore and reported EBITDA grew 78% with margin at 22.2%, up about 520 bps YoY. PAT rose 81% YoY to INR335 crore, with effective tax rate near 24%. US Generics grew 72% YoY, with base portfolio growth of 23% excluding new launches including bosutinib. Management raised FY27 consolidated growth guidance to 20-25% on stronger US and API outlook, and said India branded business should reach market-level growth within two to three quarters.

financial_highlights.change: about +520 bps YoY (from 17%); reported EBITDA +78% YoY
EBITDA margin +255 bps; reported EBITDA +51% YoY

segments.name: India branded business
segments.commentary: Grew 14% YoY in Q2; Human Health returned to double-digit growth at 11%. Specialty portfolio grew about 200 bps ahead of the Indian pharmaceutical market, while acute remains a drag.

segments.name: Animal Health
segments.commentary: Grew 23% YoY in Q2 FY27; management cites a CAGR above 20% over the last 5-7 years.

segments.name: US Generics
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 72% YoY; base business grew 23% excluding new launches including bosutinib. Three launches, five ANDAs filed and one approval in the quarter.

segments.name: US Branded (Alembic Therapeutics)
segments.commentary: Contributed close to 3% of total US revenue in Q2; about 4 products, with Pivya in a J-shaped ramp. Breakeven targeted by end-CY2026 or first half of next year.

segments.name: Ex-US
segments.commentary: Grew 12% YoY; direct presence being strengthened in Europe, LatAm and select ASEAN markets.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Volume-led growth of 39% YoY, including certain CMO deliveries to key customers; FY27 guidance raised to at least high-teens growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth raised to about 20-25% from mid-teens; includes expected normalisation of exclusivity-led sales.
US business now expected to grow up to 40% YoY for FY27.
API now expected to grow at least high-teens for FY27.
India branded expected to grow in line with market and get close to double digits; ex-US expected at mid-teens (both unchanged).

Gross margin guided at 70-75%; EBITDA margin for H2 expected to hold near H1 level of about 22%, with management saying high-teens full-year EBITDA margin was agreed in Q&A; longer term management aims towards around 20% EBITDA margin in FY28-29.
US branded dilution of 150-200 bps to margin on a full-year basis, unchanged; drag expected to end in FY28.
US generics growth for FY28 expected at about 10-12%, per management, if launches pan out.
Over 30 US launches expected over next 18 months, roughly a quarter being FTF or shared day-1 opportunities.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR250 crore; major capex cycle described as behind the company.
Focus shifts to debottlenecking and incremental line additions with no significant new greenfield investment, aiming to improve asset turns and returns.
Utilisation of existing facilities has ramped up; management sees visibility of continued operating leverage.
US branded field force at about 30-35 reps versus a target of 40-45; India field force held constant.
Line shutdown in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 for ophthalmics capacity expansion caused a minor blip.
demand_pricing: India Q2 growth: volume-led, with price and new products; management says growth roughly 50-50 between price and volume.
Chronic segment grew across almost all divisions; acute still lagging and expected to take a couple of quarters to recover.
Bosutinib sales well ahead of expectations; US exclusivity ends end-November 2026, after which outcome is uncertain.
Management says crude-driven cost increases were broadly offset by rupee depreciation in Q2.
Freight and logistics costs for India-to-US shipments rose from the March quarter as shipping lines and costs expanded.
Ophthalmics described as a strong franchise where Alembic is among the top 1-2 players; derm is more competitive but high EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-bosutinib, how did US sales perform and was bosutinib above expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Base portfolio grew 23% excluding new launches; bosutinib was far above expectations, and Q1 ex-bosutinib growth was in the mid-20s.

qa_highlights.question: Will India move in line with IPM in H2, and what is the cost and margin outlook including Pivya drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Chronic is outpacing IPM and acute should reach IPM within a couple of quarters. Employee and other costs rose on US branded expansion and freight; H1 EBITDA margin about 22% expected to hold in H2; Pivya/US branded drag guided at 150-200 bps for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin move outside the 70-75% range as India mix improves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects gross margin to stay in the 70-75% range; new-launch mix will influence it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the India business and its profitability as growth recovers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to reach IPM in the next couple of quarters with flat field force, which should lift PCPM and gradually improve margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DifGen deal structure and what does Alembic gain?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a licensing deal across 20-plus products on a profit-share basis; DifGen develops and mostly manufactures, while Alembic handles marketing and front-end. Contributions start from FY28; portfolio covers around $5 billion US reference market.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 US growth outlook and branded breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY28 US growth of about 10-12% if launches pan out. US branded to break even in the first half of next year; the company has an internal branded target but no guidance yet.

risks_watch: Bosutinib exclusivity ends end-November 2026; post-exclusivity erosion is uncertain and FY28 US growth guidance depends on new launches.
US branded ramp is slow (J-shaped curve for Pivya); breakeven timing depends on prescription trends and rep expansion.
Freight, crude and shipping-line costs could pressure gross margin; currency depreciation has offset these so far.
Acute India portfolio still lagging the market; leadership and execution changes must deliver IPM-level growth.
Working capital elevated from US launch receivables; expected to unwind over the next few quarters.
Sustainability of gross margin and EBITDA margin on normalisation of exclusivity-led sales.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter and the raised FY27 guidance, with explicit caution on the US branded ramp, acute India recovery and post-exclusivity US sales. Management was evasive on product-level forecasts (Uptravi, Toviaz, Pivya prescription counts) and declined to disclose growth splits beyond directional statements.
key_quotes: Our strong performance in the first half gives us greater confidence in the outlook for the second half of FY27.
Reflecting the stronger outlook for the U.S. and API, we are raising our FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to about 20% to 25% from the mid-teens indicated last quarter.
I think there's still a definite ramp-up required in this part of the business.
We expect the acute portfolio to improve progressively over the coming quarters as well.

adds.what: Debottlenecking and incremental line additions (no significant greenfield); ophthalmics capacity expansion line shutdown in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27

growth.why: FY27 consolidated growth raised to about 20-25% from mid-teens, with US business up to 40% and API at least high-teens; delivery backed by Q2 US generics (+72%) and 30+ launches over 18 months, plus ramped-up utilisation, but no specific new capacity numbers were given beyond debottlenecking.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 22.2% (up about 520 bps YoY) and H1 about 22%; H2 guided to hold near 22%, with gross margin guided at 70-75%, though US branded drag of 150-200 bps for FY27 and freight costs weigh.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says the major capex cycle is behind it (H1 FY27 capex about INR250 crore) with focus on debottlenecking and incremental lines, no significant greenfield; utilisation has ramped up but no new capacity numbers given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 consolidated growth raised to 20-25%, US up to 40%, API at least high-teens, and India volumes near half of 14% branded growth; backed by 30+ US launches expected over 18 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new greenfield capex planned and major cycle described as complete; utilisation has ramped up, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled but debottlenecking and line additions could be announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 consolidated growth raised to about 20-25% from mid-teens, with US up to 40% and API at least high-teens, which management framed as a raise on stronger outlook.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bosutinib exclusivity ends end-November 2026 with uncertain post-exclusivity erosion, US branded ramp is J-shaped, and freight and shipping costs rose from the March quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Over 30 US launches expected over next 18 months (about a quarter FTF or shared day-1), with three launches in Q2 and five ANDAs filed; DifGen licensing contributions start from FY28 across 20-plus products.

rows.label: Bosutinib exclusivity expiry
rows.why: Bosutinib sales well ahead of expectations, but exclusivity ends end-November 2026 and post-exclusivity outcome is uncertain, so the FY28 US generics guide of 10-12% depends on launches.

rows.label: US branded (Pivya) breakeven
rows.why: US branded contributed close to 3% of US revenue in Q2 with Pivya in a J-shaped ramp; management guides breakeven by end-CY2026 or first half of next year, with 150-200 bps FY27 margin drag ending in FY28.

rows.label: Working capital unwind
rows.why: Net debt INR1,236 crore (under 1x FY EBITDA) with elevated working capital from US launch receivables that management expects to unwind over the next few quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on the raised FY27 guide, bosutinib outperformance and H2 margin hold at about 22%, but cautious on the slow US branded ramp, acute India recovery and post-exclusivity US sales; it was evasive on product-level forecasts such as Pivya and Uptravi prescription counts.
